This suggests that individuals who maintain stable savings levels (SAMESAVE = 1) tend to have higher BMI compared to those whose savings levels change (SAMESAVE = 0). The relationship is statistically significant (p-value = 0.00077), indicating that time preference, as measured by savings behavior, may influence BMI in this demographic group.
